starters.text:
Starter Python
Week 1 / Session 1. Complete the setup block first. Paste only the code below into checks.py. Indentation
matters.
CHECKS = [
 {"site":"alpha.example","minute":"14:00","status":200,"latency_ms":120},
 {"site":"beta.example","minute":"14:00","status":200,"latency_ms":180},
 {"site":"alpha.example","minute":"14:05","status":200,"latency_ms":130},
 {"site":"beta.example","minute":"14:05","status":503,"latency_ms":900},
 {"site":"beta.example","minute":"14:10","status":503,"latency_ms":950}
]
# Rule: status >= 400 means failure.
# Worked example
def count_checks(checks):
    total = 0
    for check in checks:
        total += 1
    return total
print(count_checks(CHECKS))
Expected result
Running .venv\Scripts\python.exe checks.py prints 5. The next exercise copies count_checks and adds the
failure condition.
The fixture is invented. status >= 400 means failure in the early CLI exercises. The backend later uses UP
for 2xx and DOWN otherwise.

starters.text:
Starter PostgreSQL
Create a new Sitewatch capstone folder/repository, separate from sitewatch-lab.
CREATE TABLE sites (
 id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
 name TEXT NOT NULL,
 url TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE
);
CREATE TABLE checks (
 id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
 site_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES sites(id),
 observed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
 status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(status IN ('UP','DOWN')),
 reason TEXT NOT NULL,
 status_code INTEGER CHECK(status_code BETWEEN 100 AND 599),
